ReferenceLabels.description:
One reading of one article. Every field is empty when the set is built.

The vocabularies are `config/taxonomy.json`, so nothing here enumerates a
member: a label is a slug the taxonomy names, and adding a word to the
taxonomy may not be a schema change (plan 23 section 0.1). Three of the five
label fields name a vocabulary `config/taxonomy.json` does not carry yet -
`article_kind`, `stances` and `sentiment` - so the 2026-09-13 pass took them
from plan 23 rows #8, #10 and #11, and `backend/utilities/
label_reference_dataset.py` is where that list sits until those rows land.

**`stances` is keyed and valued in slugs, which the plan's own spelling is
not.** `Slug` admits the hyphen and refuses the underscore, so the axis is
`stance-on-change` and the decline is `not-applicable`. Plan 23 row #10
writes both with underscores and row #9's token measurement was taken on
that spelling; one of the two has to move, and it is not this one.

`reference_summary` **has a writer from 2026-09-13** and it is the labeller.
It is a reference for classification labels and is **never** a faithfulness
reference - the human faithfulness ledger was dropped and only its contract
kept (plan 23 row #P2 decision 6, owner, 2026-09-10).

article_kind.description: What kind of writing it is - a report, an analysis, a notice.
article_kind.title: Article Kind

definition_version.description: Which `config/taxonomy.json` definition text the label was taken against. A label taken against last month's definition measures a different question.
definition_version.title: Definition Version

desk.description: Which desk the article belongs to, read from the text.
desk.title: Desk

labelled_by.description: Who read it. A person, never a model.
labelled_by.title: Labelled By

lenses.description: Every lens the article carries. May be empty.
lenses.title: Lenses

reference_summary.description: The labeller's own summary of the article. A reference for classification labels, never a faithfulness reference - plan 23 row #P2 decision 6.
reference_summary.title: Reference Summary

sentiment.description: Sentiment about one named subject, not about the article.
sentiment.title: Sentiment

stances.description: One stance per political question the article takes a position on.
stances.title: Stances

ReferenceLabels.title: ReferenceLabels

changelog.change: Description only, on three sentences the first labelling pass made false: `reference_summary` has a writer, `second_labels` holds the same labeller's alternative reading rather than an independent second rating, and the module no longer claims no model wrote a field here.
changelog.why: The pass of 2026-09-13 filled all 641 rows at the owner's direction and recorded `labelled_by` of `human` (owner decision, `CLAUDE.md` section 0). Who wrote a label is the fact every number taken on this set rests on, so a contract asserting the opposite is worse than one that says nothing. No field moved, so no payload needs a migration.

changelog.change: Initial shape: the article's identity and provenance, the text file's digest and word count, and two empty label slots - one per rater.
changelog.why: Plan 23 measures a classifier against a frozen labelled set, and the set needs a declared shape before anything writes one (Guardrail #3). The split is deliberately absent: `splits/dev.txt` and `splits/test.txt` are the split, and a copy of it here is a second thing that can disagree. `second_labels` is here from the first commit because row #P3 double-labels 60 dev items for a Cohen's kappa, and a field added later would make that a schema argument in the middle of a labelling pass.

article_sha256.description: sha256 of `articles/<url_key>.txt`. What detects a text edited in place, which would silently move what a label was taken against.
article_sha256.title: Article Sha256

article_words.description: Words in the article file. Recomputed by `verify`, never trusted.
article_words.title: Article Words

canonical_url.description: What `url_key` is derived from, never trusted from a payload.
canonical_url.title: Canonical Url

fetched_on.description: The day the text was taken. The set is frozen from here.
fetched_on.title: Fetched On

published_date.description: The day the article was published.
published_date.title: Published Date

sanitizer_version.description: Which sanitizer the text crossed the trust boundary through.
sanitizer_version.title: Sanitizer Version

second_labels.description: A second reading of the same article. On the 2026-09-13 pass it is the same labeller's alternative reading, which is NOT an independent second rating and may not be used for a Cohen's kappa. Null is not a disagreement.

source_domain.description: The registrable domain, which is the unit the split is drawn on. Two articles from one outlet share boilerplate, a house style and often a wire original, so a split that separates rows rather than outlets flatters every number taken on it.
source_domain.title: Source Domain

source_url.description: The address the feed carried, kept so a person can open it.
source_url.title: Source Url

url_key.description: sha256 of the canonical URL, recomputed on read. It is the join to `splits/*.txt`, to `articles/<url_key>.txt`, and to every collection this set must not overlap.
url_key.title: Url Key

vertical.description: The vertical the pipeline published it under, kept as context.
vertical.title: Vertical
